title: Siri AI Developer Preview Lets iOS, iPadOS, and macOS Apps Integrate with Siri
gist: Apple shipped a Siri AI Developer Preview in its 27.3 OS betas, letting any app expose content and actions to the rebuilt Siri AI via App Intents and chain actions via a new Skills feature. Access is limited to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers, usage limits may apply with premium access planned, and Siri AI is unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS.

themes.theme: Siri AI platform opening to developers

insights.claim: Apple released the Siri AI Developer Preview in the 27.3 beta releases of its operating systems, letting developers and apps integrate with the assistant and hand off actions to it, with access restricted to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Marks the start of Apple's third-party agentic assistant ecosystem, a key test of its AI strategy.
insights.locator: Apple released the Siri AI Developer Preview

insights.claim: Apple describes Siri AI as an entirely new version of its assistant that is profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Apple is positioning a full assistant rebuild rather than incremental upgrades, raising stakes on execution.
insights.quote: profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal

insights.claim: Any app can bring its content and actions into Siri AI using App Intents, tapping capabilities such as personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, and natural language.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Reusing an existing framework lowers developer adoption friction, speeding ecosystem breadth.

insights.claim: A new Skills feature lets developers teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience, supporting complex multi-step requests.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Multi-action orchestration turns Siri into an agent layer above apps, shifting where user intent is captured.
insights.quote: teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience

insights.claim: Siri AI requests that do not name an app are routed to the foreground app, the app with an active Live Activity, or the app previously mentioned in the conversation, while background apps only receive requests that explicitly mention their name.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Routing rules favor foreground/recently used apps, influencing which apps capture assistant-driven engagement.
insights.locator: If a request does not specify an app name

insights.claim: Siri AI requests can span multiple apps, such as finding content in one app, sending it to another, and performing an action there.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Cross-app agentic flows could disintermediate individual app UIs, a second-order risk for app-centric business models.
insights.locator: Requests can also include actions across apps

insights.claim: An early Reddit tester reported that Siri AI works as advertised when intents and parameters have good descriptions, saying this is what Siri should have been since 26.0.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Early positive developer sentiment, though anecdotal, suggests the rebuild may address Siri's long-standing capability gap.
insights.quote: If you include a good description on your intent and parameters, Siri can figure it out.
insights.locator: Commenting on Apple's announcement, Reddit user

insights.claim: A Reddit commenter argued Apple's choice to build on App Intents was better than Google's approach of a separate agent skills SDK instead of reusing Android intents.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Developer-friction differences could shape which mobile platform builds a richer agent ecosystem first.
insights.quote: Doing it via app intents was the right move.

insights.claim: All Apple Intelligence features, including Siri AI, may be subject to usage limits, with extended premium access planned for the future.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Hints at a potential paid/premium AI tier, a new monetization lever for Apple services revenue.
insights.locator: All Apple Intelligence features, including Siri AI

insights.claim: Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS, which affects EU-based developers.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Regulatory friction keeps Apple's flagship AI features out of a major market, limiting near-term reach.
insights.locator: All Apple Intelligence features, including Siri AI
